title: Store Tricks That Make You Spend More (You Only Went for Milk)
alts: Why You Always Spend More Than You Planned at the Store
You Went in for Milk and Spent $87. Here's Why.
line1: Why do you always spend more at the store? Dave went in for $3.49 of milk and walked out with $87 of stuff. Here's how stores do it.
summary: Dave goes to the store for one carton of milk and walks out with $87 of stuff. We break down the grocery store psychology behind it: why the milk is always at the back, how bigger carts make you buy more, eye-level shelves and FTC-studied slotting fees, end caps, $9.99 charm pricing and the left-digit effect, fake 'was' prices under the FTC's deceptive pricing guides, BOGO and '10 for $10' anchors, free-shipping thresholds, loyalty apps and personalized pricing, and the checkout candy trap. Then we show simple ways to walk out with just the milk.
